itinerary.cal: North Cascades National Park requires a wilderness permit for overnight camping in Terror/Crescent Creek Basins; the route is typically climbed July-September when the Barrier's grassy ledges are snow-free and stable.

days.note: From the Goodell Creek trailhead, follow an old roadbed and climbers' path up Terror Creek through timber to treeline, then boulder-hop/scramble to a camp near 5,800 ft in Terror Basin, just below the saddle leading toward the Barrier. This mirrors the standard Southern Pickets approach day used for Inspiration, Terror, Degenhardt, etc.
days.title: Approach to Terror Basin
days.objective: Establish first high camp at ~5,800 ft in Terror Basin

days.note: A short but serious day: sustained Class 3 scrambling up loose, grassy ledges to the Barrier crest (~6,400-6,600 ft), exposed but well-traveled, then down the far side into Crescent Creek Basin to camp near 6,200 ft below the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn massif. Parties often arrive early enough to scout the col or bag an easy nearby summit in the afternoon.
days.title: Cross the Barrier into Crescent Creek Basin
days.objective: Cross 'The Barrier' and set up camp near Crescent Creek Basin (~6,200 ft)

days.note: An alpine-start day climbing roughly an hour up scrambling terrain from camp to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, then following Ottohorn's east ridge and connecting terrain (short roped/low-5th pitches where the ridge steepens) over to Frenzel Spitz's summit block. Many parties link Ottohorn and/or Himmelhorn onto the same day since all three share the same col approach.
days.title: Summit push: Ottohorn - Frenzel Spitz

schedule.label: Leave Crescent Creek Basin camp
schedule.detail: Light rack, rope, and water only; boots/approach shoes for the scramble to the col.

schedule.label: Reach Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col
schedule.detail: Roughly an hour of scrambling from camp; can be loose Class 3-5 late-season.

schedule.label: Climb Ottohorn's east ridge
schedule.detail: Short low-5th-class pitches to gain the ridge crest.

schedule.label: Traverse to Frenzel Spitz
schedule.detail: Connecting ridge/scramble terrain between the two summits.

schedule.label: Summit Frenzel Spitz
schedule.detail: Optional continuation to Himmelhorn if time and weather allow.

schedule.label: Back at Crescent Creek Basin camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and col descent, rappelling short steps as needed.

days.objective: Climb Ottohorn's east ridge to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col and continue to Frenzel Spitz

days.note: Pack up Crescent Creek Basin camp, re-cross the Barrier back into Terror Basin, and continue the long descent down Terror Creek to the trailhead. Fit parties do this in one long push, similar in reverse to Days 1-2 combined; some choose to split it into two shorter days if the group is tired or weather is closing in.
days.title: Exit: back over the Barrier to the trailhead
days.objective: Break camp, re-cross the Barrier, and hike out to Goodell Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote, non-technical-camp-to-technical-summit trip: roughly 4 days and ~18 miles round trip with ~7,600 ft of cumulative gain, most of it on Day 1 and the Day 4 exit, bracketing a short but serious Barrier crossing and a roped scramble/ridge day to tag the summit.

waypoints.name: Goodell Creek / Upper Goodell Group Camp trailhead (SR-20, Newhalem)
waypoints.note: Park off SR-20 near Newhalem at Goodell Creek Campground/road; NPS wilderness permit required for overnight camping in Terror/Crescent Creek Basins.
waypoints.directions: Drive Highway 20 to Newhalem and park at the Goodell Creek Campground and trailhead just off the highway. An NPS wilderness permit is required for overnight camping in the Terror and Crescent Creek Basins, so arrange that before you head in.

waypoints.name: Cairn - Old Roadbed / Terror Basin Fork
waypoints.note: Old logging roadbed ends here; a cairn (replacing an older rock arrow) marks the unmaintained boot path climbing steeply south of Terror Creek toward Terror Basin.
waypoints.directions: Follow the old roadbed and climbers' path up the Goodell Creek valley for about four miles, gaining only around 1,000 ft. Fill water at the junction: this is the last easy, reliable source before the climb steepens.

waypoints.name: Terror Creek Log Jam Crossing
waypoints.note: Cross Terror Creek on a log jam; the exact crossing point shifts year to year and can require wading or bushwhacking upstream in high water.
waypoints.directions: Leave the roadbed at the cairn on the unmaintained path cutting uphill and to the right; it reaches Terror Creek within a few hundred yards, before any of the real climbing begins.

waypoints.name: Terror Basin
waypoints.note: Gravelly, wildflower basin with established tent sites and multiple streams; the standard base camp for Southern Pickets objectives, roughly 3+ hours in.
waypoints.directions: Past the creek the boot path turns relentlessly steep, gaining roughly 4,000-4,700 ft in well under three horizontal miles through old-growth and brush; expect head-high slide alder and devil's club depending on the season and snow year. It breaks out of timber near 5,000-5,200 ft onto heather benches, slabs and snowfields. The path is boot-beaten but often faint, and there is no dependable water between the creek and the basin.

waypoints.name: The Barrier
waypoints.note: Loose, exposed low-5th-class ridge crossing over a moat divides Terror Basin from Crescent Creek Basin; classic unstable 'Pickets Class 3' terrain, harder late season.
waypoints.directions: From the tent sites, climb up-basin roughly 700 ft to the north-northwest to reach the crest of the divide. The ground is grassy ledges and loose blocks, and it is the one stretch of the approach where a slip has real consequences.

waypoints.name: Crescent Creek Basin Camp
waypoints.note: Flat camping area below Mount Terror used as the high camp for Ottohorn, Himmelhorn, and Frenzel Spitz objectives.
waypoints.directions: Drop about 500 ft off the far side on mixed snow and talus, steeply at first, then traverse for roughly an hour into the basin under the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn massif to reach the flat ground used for camping.

waypoints.name: Ottohorn-Himmelhorn Col
waypoints.note: Gain the col from Crescent Creek Basin (snow-filled and straightforward early season, loose tricky 5th class if melted out); the South Route ridge to Frenzel Spitz departs from here.
waypoints.directions: From the basin camp it is about 1,400 ft and roughly an hour of climbing up to the crest. This Crescent Creek side is the friendly side of the col, loose but moderate 3rd and 4th class; the side that guards it from the north is sustained loose 5th class, so do not plan on reversing it that way.

waypoints.name: Frenzel Spitz Summit
waypoints.note: True summit gained via 5.6 rock along the connecting ridge from the col; descend by reversing the ridge and downclimbing/rappelling back to the col.
waypoints.directions: Do not try to follow the crest across. From the col, downclimb roughly 500 ft of broken, frequently snow- or ice-covered ground onto the Frenzel Spitz side to reach the foot of the South Route, then climb its rock at about 5.6 back up to the top. The small net height difference between col and summit hides a full descent and re-ascent, so budget the time for it; the step below the col is commonly rappelled from natural anchors on the way back.

before.overview: Frenzel Spitz (7,440 ft) is the smallest and most remote of the three-summit Crescent Creek Spires cluster in the Southern Pickets, tucked directly beneath the north face of Ottohorn on the ridge connecting the Southern and Northern Pickets. Because it sits off the main crest and is only reachable after first gaining Ottohorn via the Ottohorn–Himmelhorn col, it is one of the more inaccessible technical summits in the North Cascades — it wasn't climbed until September 10, 1961, on the same expedition that put up several other Crescent Creek Spires first ascents. In 2003, Wayne Wallace, Mark Bunker, and Colin Haley used it as the endpoint of a high traverse of all the major Southern Pickets summits (from Little Mac Spire to Frenzel Spitz), a line that had not been repeated as of the early 2010s.
before.pro_needs: A light rock rack sufficient for 5.6 terrain, plus standard glacier travel gear (axe, crampons, rope) for the connecting ridge/snowfield sections between Ottohorn and Frenzel Spitz.
before.approach: Start at the Goodell Creek trailhead (~600 ft, off Hwy 20 near Newhalem, North Cascades NP/Ross Lake NRA). Follow the old roadbed/climbers' path paralleling Goodell Creek for about 4 miles, gaining only ~1,000 ft, to a junction around 1,700 ft marked by a stone/rock arrow, post, and large cairn — this is the standard jump-off for every Southern Pickets objective and the last easy, reliable water before the climb steepens. Here the unmaintained Terror Creek climbers' trail cuts uphill to the right and turns relentlessly steep: a boot-beaten but often faint path gains roughly 4,000-4,700 ft in well under 3 horizontal miles through old-growth forest and brush (expect head-high slide alder/devil's club depending on season and snow year) before breaking out of timber around 5,000-5,200 ft onto heather benches, slabs, and snowfields. From treeline, rather than stopping at Terror Basin (the camp used for McMillan/Inspiration/Terror objectives), continue a rising traverse west/northwest staying near the 5,800-6,400 ft band into Crescent Creek Basin — the standard high camp for Frenzel Spitz, Himmelhorn, Ottohorn, and the Chopping Block, reached via a steep initial drop into the basin on mixed snow/talus followed by a roughly one-hour traverse. From camp, climb east/northeast onto the ridge to gain the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col; the south (Crescent Creek) side of this col is the comparatively friendlier side — loose but moderate 3rd/4th class scrambling — in contrast to the sustained loose 5th-class terrain that guards it from the north. From the col, downclimb/scramble roughly 500 ft down broken, frequently snow- or ice-covered terrain on the Frenzel Spitz side to reach the base of the South Route proper. There is no dependable water above the Terror Creek junction until snowmelt or tarns near camp, so carry enough for the ~4,500+ ft, multi-hour climb in between; the ~18-mile round-trip distance reflects that this is realistically a long day-and-a-half approach with a basin camp, not a single push.

approach_variants.name: Goodell Creek and the Terror Creek path, past Terror Basin to a Crescent Creek Basin camp, then over the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col
approach_variants.notes:
Start at the Goodell Creek trailhead at about 600 ft off Hwy 20 near Newhalem. Follow the old roadbed and climbers' path along Goodell Creek for about 4 miles, gaining only about 1,000 ft, to a junction around 1,700 ft marked by a stone arrow, a post and a large cairn. That junction is the standard jump-off for EVERY Southern Pickets objective and the last easy, reliable water before the climb steepens.

The unmaintained Terror Creek climbers' trail cuts uphill to the right and turns relentlessly steep, gaining roughly 4,000-4,700 ft in well under 3 horizontal miles through old-growth forest and brush, with head-high slide alder and devil's club depending on the season, before breaking out of timber around 5,000-5,200 ft onto heather benches, slabs and snowfields.

From treeline, rather than stopping at Terror Basin, continue a rising traverse west-northwest staying near the 5,800-6,400 ft band into Crescent Creek Basin, reached via a steep initial drop into the basin on mixed snow and talus followed by roughly an hour of traversing.
hazards: Head-high slide alder and devil's club on a relentlessly steep unmaintained path
No dependable water for roughly 4,500 ft of climbing
Broken, frequently snow- or ice-covered ground on the 500 ft descent to the route's base
The north side of the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col is a rappel proposition with glacier and moat terrain below it
Glacier edges near the col have been described as unable to hold body weight late season
approach_variants.baseFinding:
THIS ROUTE IS REACHED BY GOING OVER A COL AND THEN DOWN THE FAR SIDE, AND THE DOWNHILL IS THE TEST. From the Crescent Creek Basin camp, climb east or northeast onto the ridge to gain the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col, then DOWNCLIMB AND SCRAMBLE ROUGHLY 500 FT down broken, frequently snow- or ice-covered ground on the FRENZEL SPITZ side to reach the base of the South Route proper. If you are still on the col, or above it, you have not started.

WHICH SIDE OF THE COL IS WHICH, AND IT IS THE ONE FACT THAT KEEPS PARTIES OUT OF TROUBLE HERE: the SOUTH, Crescent Creek side of that col is the friendly side, loose but moderate 3rd and 4th class scrambling. The NORTH side is sustained loose 5th class and drops into a broken couloir and glacier and moat terrain, and parties commonly need a rappel to get down it. If the ground below you needs a rope to descend, you are on the north side and you are heading for the Mustard Glacier, not Frenzel Spitz.

ARRIVAL AT CAMP, WHICH IS THE OTHER PLACE THIS DAY GETS LOST: Crescent Creek Basin, not Terror Basin. Terror Basin is where the McMillan, Inspiration and Terror parties stop. The Frenzel Spitz, Himmelhorn, Ottohorn and Chopping Block camp is the NEXT basin west, reached by holding the 5,800-6,400 ft band and traversing about an hour further. Stopping at the first flat ground above treeline puts you a basin short.

NO DEPENDABLE WATER above the Terror Creek junction until snowmelt or tarns near camp; carry enough for 4,500-plus ft of climbing in between.

before.descent_text: Reverse the approach line: from the Frenzel Spitz summit, downclimb/scramble back down to the base of the connecting gully and climb back up the ~500 ft of broken, loose terrain to regain the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col. From the col, the descent onto the north side drops into a broken couloir and glacier/moat terrain — anchors reported here are natural (a pin, sling, and/or nut equalized in a crack or around a block), not bolted or chained, so be ready to build or back up your own and treat any fixed tat as suspect. Parties commonly need one rappel to get down the steepest ice/rock step directly below the col; a single 60m rope has been reported as sufficient, though in icy or early-season conditions some parties have needed a second, shorter rappel or have downclimbed a lower-angle step instead of rappelling it. Below the rappel, expect further downclimbing across broken glacier and moat terrain — this is a real late-season hazard: test snow edges carefully before committing weight, and be ready to use an ice axe to climb out of moat pits, since the glacier edges near the col have been described as unable to hold body weight. Once back down into Crescent Creek Basin, retrace the approach traverse and descend the steep climbers' path back down to the Goodell Creek roadbed and trailhead.

weather.typical: Remote alpine climate: needs dry rock and stable weather; summer is the reliable window, winter is severe and rarely attempted
weather.probability: Afternoon thunderstorms and fast-moving weather systems are common risks for a remote, multi-day Cascades objective; fall brings cold, stormy conditions that can arrive early

seasonal_hazards.exposure: Significant - loose rock, exposure, and remoteness; a fall or injury on Grade III terrain this far from a trailhead is a serious, likely multi-day evacuation given the North Cascades NP backcountry setting

avalanche.zone: N/A - non-glaciated summer rock route; falls within the general North Cascades NWAC forecast zone, but NWAC does not issue forecasts during the Jul-Sep climbing season for this route

seasonal_hazards.crevasses: The col-to-route connection on the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col's north side crosses broken glacier and moat terrain - glacier edges near the col can be unable to hold body weight and an ice axe is needed to climb out of moat pits, especially late season. The technical rock climbing on Frenzel Spitz itself is not glaciated.

before.permit: North Cascades NP complex: no permit for day climbs; all overnight backcountry stays require a backcountry permit (reserve on Recreation.gov or walk-up at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center).

access.fees: $10 per person plus a $6 Recreation.gov reservation fee for advance backcountry permits; climbers 15 and under are free.
access.notes: 60% of sites are reservable in advance via Recreation.gov (2026 lottery Mar 2–13); the remaining 40% are walk-up, obtained in person the day before at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.
access.rules: Camp only within your assigned cross-country zone (Terror Basin / Crescent Creek Basin); no campfires; pack out all trash; group size in the Crescent Creek zone is limited (small-party capacity).
access.permit: A backcountry/wilderness permit is required year-round for any overnight stay in Terror Basin or Crescent Creek Basin. This area falls in a Ross Lake NRA cross-country zone that requires in-person pickup: reserve dates in advance on Recreation.gov, watch the mandatory safety video, then collect the printed/signed permit in person at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount (walk-up/email permits are not issued for this destination).
access.closures: SR-20 to the Goodell Creek/Newhalem trailhead is open year-round — the highway's seasonal winter closure gate is much farther east near Ross Lake/Washington Pass and does not affect this approach. Check current NPS trail/backcountry alerts for storm washouts on the Goodell Creek roadbed.
access.landManager: North Cascades National Park (NPS) — North Cascades National Park Service Complex, Wilderness District; permits issued at the Wilderness Information Center, 7280 Ranger Station Rd, Marblemount, WA.
access.land_manager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
access.passRequired: No park entrance fee or pass is required — North Cascades NP is one of the few fee-free NPS units; only the backcountry camping permit above applies.

overnight_permit.what: North Cascades NP backcountry permit for the cross-country zone, with a fee
overnight_permit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, then get the permit by email or in person at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center; walk-up permits are issued there the day of or the day before.

pro_tips: Climb all three horns from one camp
